newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says PLO should halt "delaying tactics".
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says PLO should halt "delaying tactics".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday a deal with the PLO on a long-overdue troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron was in reach if Palestinians stopped using "delaying tactics".
"There has been some progress, even considerable, in the negotiations," Netanyahu told Jewish fundraisers from abroad in a Jerusalem address.
"I hope that they have made a decision to stop using delaying tactics, to negotiate in good faith and to complete an agreement that can serve, I think, the purposes of both sides."
But Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Sunday two weeks of intensive talks had yielded no progress on the Hebron pullout, agreed to by Israel's previous government in a peace deal last year.
"There is no progress in the negotiations," Arafat told Israel Radio. He said Palestinians wanted Israel to implement not only the Hebron withdrawal, but all other outstanding Israeli commitments.

Under interim peace deals, Israel committed itself, among other things, to release Palestinian prisoners, open a safe passage between Palestinian-ruled zones in the West Bank and Gaza, and to further troop pullbacks in rural West Bank areas.
Leaders of Israeli and Palestinian negotiating teams were meeting in Tel Aviv on Sunday ahead of a resumption of formal talks on Monday in Israel's Red Sea port city of Eilat.

Israel delayed the Hebron redeployment, due last March, after a spree of Islamic bus bombings in the Jewish state. The right-wing Netanyahu put withdrawal plans on hold after he ousted Israel's Labour-party government in elections last May.

The Israeli prime minister wants added measures to ensure the security of 400 settlers who live in heavily armed compounds amid 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron. Palestinians reject any renegotiation of the signed accord.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, touring Hebron on Sunday, denied Israel had halted peace moves.
"We are for furthering the peace process. We did not stop the process. The one who stopped it is not us," Mordechai told reporters.
